title: One fixed fee per order
hook: The same goods can produce different totals when a fee repeats.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Separate per-order charges from per-item costs.

misconception: Equal merchandise subtotals guarantee equal checkout totals.
objective: Separate per-order charges from per-item costs.

claims.text: The same goods total €24. Each order adds a fictional €4 delivery fee. Scaled model; same goods; €4/order; no discounts.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by this lesson's declared expressions; each card prints its working in plain words. At Orders=2, A=€32.00 and B=€28.00. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["+",24,["*",4,"x"]]; B=28; x denotes Orders. At x=2, A=32, B=28. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md. Reset to unverified by demo-builder 2026-10-15 (v2, company/decisions/2026-10-15-lifehacks-r11-fix-plan.md): v2 stage: plain-words readouts (TP-7a), no 'Full scale' label (TP-7b), money to 2 decimals (TP-7c); A=["+", 24, ["*", 4, "x"]], B=["+", 24, ["*", 4, 1]], variable {"label": "Orders", "start": 2, "min": 1, "max": 6, "unit": "", "step": 1}. Card B now prints 24 + (4 × 1) = 28 instead of a bare 28; the receipts draw one €4.00 fee line per order (A: 2 at the start, B: 1). Values unchanged: A = 24 + 4×2 = €32, B = €28. | FC pass 51 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15, W-1101): VERIFIED. Own run: at 2 orders A = 24 + 4 × 2 = €32.00, B = 24 + 4 × 1 = €28.00; readouts '24 + (4 × 2)' / '24 + (4 × 1)'. The receipts print 'Goods €24.00', one 'Fee €4.00' line per order (2 and 1 at the start, up to 6) and the total. Note: this receipt prints exact amounts, so the claim's fixed-scale sentence describes no picture in this lesson; harmless, but the builder may trim it. Record: company/reviews/lh-split-order-fixed-fee/2026-10-15-fact-check.md, Pass 51.
